title: Deep Blue lost in 1996, then won in 1997
summary: IBM's chess machine lost a match in 1996. An upgraded Deep Blue won the 1997 rematch 3.5 to 2.5.

beats.say: A chess machine lost in nineteen ninety six, then won the rematch.
IBM designed Deep Blue to play chess.
In nineteen ninety six, Deep Blue one lost the match four to two.
The nineteen ninety seven machine used four hundred eighty chess chips.
It could evaluate about two hundred million positions every second.
In May nineteen ninety seven, the rematch ran six games.
It won two, drew three, and lost one.
The deciding sixth game lasted only nineteen moves.
Final score: three and a half to two and a half.
Four hundred eighty chips. Three and a half points.

claims.note: Britannica: Deep Blue won the 1997 rematch 3.5-2.5 (two wins, three draws)
Campbell et al., Deep Blue: a 30-node IBM RS/6000 SP
Campbell et al.: 16 chess chips per node
Britannica: could evaluate 200 million chess positions per second
Britannica: won the deciding sixth game in 19 moves

facts.claim: IBM's Deep Blue won the six-game 1997 rematch 3.5 to 2.5 with two wins and three draws, and took the deciding sixth game in 19 moves
facts.note: Britannica, Deep Blue: won 3.5-2.5, two wins and three draws; sixth game won in 19 moves

facts.claim: Deep Blue could evaluate 200 million chess positions per second
facts.note: Britannica, Deep Blue: 200 million positions per second

facts.claim: In 1996 the human champion won 4-2 against Deep Blue I, a six-game match
facts.note: Campbell, Hoane, Hsu 2002: 1996 match won 4-2 by the human champion against Deep Blue I

facts.claim: The 1997 Deep Blue was a 30-node IBM RS/6000 SP with 16 chess chips per node, 480 in total, and the rematch was played in May 1997
facts.note: Campbell et al.: 30-node RS/6000 SP, 480 single-chip chess search engines, 16 per node; rematch May 1997

youtube.hook: IBM's Deep Blue lost a match in 1996 and won the 1997 rematch 3.5 to 2.5. The 1997 machine used 480 custom chess chips.
